options: спектакль
спектакля
спектаклю
спектаклем
cases.explain: «Спектакль» is the grammatical subject of «начнется», so it stands in the nominative case.

options: тоска
тоски
тоске
тоской
cases.translation: Out of longing/anguish I cannot sit at home.
cases.explain: The preposition «от» (from/because of) governs the genitive case, giving «тоски».

cases.sentence: А меня тянет сюда к ___, как чайку.
options: озеро
озера
озеру
озером
cases.translation: And I am drawn here to the lake, like a seagull.
cases.explain: The preposition «к» (toward) governs the dative case, giving «озеру».

cases.sentence: Мария Ильинична, будьте добры, попросите вашего папашу, чтобы он распорядился отвязать ___.
options: собака
собаки
собаке
собаку
cases.translation: Maria Ilyinichna, would you be so kind as to ask your father to have the dog untied.
cases.explain: «Собаку» is the direct object of the infinitive «отвязать» (to untie), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Но мне надоело, что она носится с этим ___.
options: билетрист
билетриста
билетристу
билетристом
cases.translation: But I'm sick of her fussing over this novelist.
cases.explain: The verb «носиться с (кем-чем)» governs the instrumental case, giving «билетристом».

cases.sentence: Никогда в ___ не жил, как хотел.
options: деревня
деревни
деревне
деревню
cases.translation: I never got to live in the countryside the way I wanted.
cases.explain: The preposition «в» marking location governs the prepositional case here, giving «деревне».

reading.ru: Отчего вы всегда ходите в черном?
reading.question: What does Medvedenko ask Masha at the very start of the play?
options: Why she always wears black
Why she is always late
Why she never smiles
Why she avoids him
reading.correct: Why she always wears black
reading.explain: The opening line is a question about why Masha always dresses in black.

reading.ru: Это траур по моей жизни.
reading.question: How does Masha explain why she wears black?
options: It is mourning for her (unhappy) life
It is the fashion in the city
Her mother told her to
It is required for her job
reading.correct: It is mourning for her (unhappy) life
reading.explain: Masha answers that it is mourning for her life, revealing her deep unhappiness.

reading.ru: Я получаю всего 23 рубля в месяц.
reading.question: How much does Medvedenko say he earns per month?
options: Only 23 rubles
100 rubles
500 rubles
Nothing, he works for free
reading.correct: Only 23 rubles
reading.explain: Medvedenko complains that he earns only 23 rubles a month.

reading.ru: Играть будет Заречная, а пьеса сочинения Константин Гаврилыча.
reading.question: Who will perform in the play, and who wrote it?
options: Zarechnaya will act, and it was written by Konstantin Gavrilovich
Masha will act, written by Medvedenko
Arkadina will act, written by Trigorin
Sorin will act, written by himself
reading.correct: Zarechnaya will act, and it was written by Konstantin Gavrilovich
reading.explain: The text states that Zarechnaya will perform, and the play was written by Konstantin Gavrilovich (Treplev).

reading.ru: От тоски не могу сидеть дома.
reading.question: Why does Masha say she cannot stay home?
options: Out of anguish/melancholy
Because her father forbids it
Because the house is too small
Because she has chores to do
reading.correct: Out of anguish/melancholy
reading.explain: Masha says that out of melancholy (toska) she cannot bear to sit at home.

reading.ru: Ваша любовь трогает меня, но я не могу отвечать взаимностью.
reading.question: How does Masha respond to Medvedenko's love for her?
options: She is touched but cannot return his feelings
She says she loves him too
She tells him to stop bothering her forever
She agrees to marry him
reading.correct: She is touched but cannot return his feelings
reading.explain: Masha tells him his love touches her, but she cannot reciprocate it.

reading.ru: Мария Ильинична, будьте добры, попросите вашего папашу, чтобы он распорядился отвязать собаку.
reading.question: What request does someone make of Masha regarding the dog?
options: To ask her father to have the dog untied
To feed the dog
To take the dog for a walk
To give the dog away
reading.correct: To ask her father to have the dog untied
reading.explain: The speaker politely asks Masha to have her father order the dog untied, since it howls.

reading.ru: Бывало, возьмешь отпуск на 28 дней и приедешь сюда, чтобы отдохнуть, и все.
reading.question: What does Sorin recall about his past vacations at the estate?
options: He used to take 28 days of leave to come rest here
He never had any vacation time
He always spent his leave in the city
He came here only once, briefly
reading.correct: He used to take 28 days of leave to come rest here
reading.explain: Sorin recalls that he used to take a 28-day leave and come here just to rest.

reading.ru: Ровно в половине девятого как раз зайдет луна.
reading.question: What timing detail does Treplev mention about the moon for the play's staging?
options: The moon will set exactly at half past eight
The sun will rise at half past eight
The play starts at half past eight
The guests arrive at half past eight
reading.correct: The moon will set exactly at half past eight
reading.explain: Treplev notes that the moon will set precisely at half past eight, timing for the outdoor stage.

reading.ru: Отец с мачехой стерегут ее, и вырваться из дому так же тяжело, как из тюрьмы.
reading.question: Why might Nina (Zarechnaya) be late for the performance?
options: Her father and stepmother guard her closely, making it hard to escape the house
She has to travel a very long distance
She is rehearsing another play
She forgot the date of the performance
reading.correct: Her father and stepmother guard her closely, making it hard to escape the house
reading.explain: The text explains that her father and stepmother watch her so closely that escaping the house is as hard as escaping prison.

reading.ru: Она уже и против меня, и против спектакля, против моей пьесы, потому что не она играет, а Заречная.
reading.question: Why is Treplev's mother (Arkadina) against his play, according to him?
options: Because Zarechnaya is acting in it instead of her
Because she thinks the play is poorly written
Because she dislikes the outdoor setting
Because she wasn't consulted about it
reading.correct: Because Zarechnaya is acting in it instead of her
reading.explain: Treplev says his mother is against the play because Zarechnaya, not she, is the one performing in it.

reading.ru: Нужно хвалить только ее одну, кричать, восхищаться ее великолепной игрой там в «Даме с камелями» или в «Чар жизни».
reading.question: According to Treplev, what does his mother demand regarding praise?
options: That only she be praised for her acting, such as in 'The Lady of the Camellias'
That the whole cast be praised equally
That critics never write about actors
That she be left alone and not discussed
reading.correct: That only she be praised for her acting, such as in 'The Lady of the Camellias'
reading.explain: Treplev complains that only she must be praised and admired for her magnificent acting, citing her roles in 'The Lady of the Camellias' and 'The Fumes of Life.'

reading.ru: И скупа, я знаю, у нее в Одессе в банке семьдесят тысяч, это я знаю, наверное.
reading.question: What does Treplev claim about his mother's wealth and stinginess?
options: She has seventy thousand in an Odessa bank yet is stingy
She has given away all her money to charity
She has no savings at all
She spends all her money on Trigorin
reading.correct: She has seventy thousand in an Odessa bank yet is stingy
reading.explain: Treplev claims his mother is stingy and has seventy thousand rubles in a bank in Odessa.

reading.ru: Меня моя мать не любит.
reading.question: What painful belief does Treplev express about his mother?
options: That his mother does not love him
That his mother has forgotten him
That his mother prefers Sorin
That his mother wants him to leave
reading.correct: That his mother does not love him
reading.explain: Treplev states plainly that his own mother does not love him.

reading.ru: Вот я и бегу, как Мапасан бежал от Эйфелевой башни, которая давила ему мозг своей пошлостью.
reading.question: What comparison does Treplev make about his own aversion to conventional theater?
options: He flees it like Maupassant fled the Eiffel Tower, which he found oppressively vulgar
He compares himself to Napoleon fleeing Russia
He compares it to fleeing a burning building
He compares it to running from a storm
reading.correct: He flees it like Maupassant fled the Eiffel Tower, which he found oppressively vulgar
reading.explain: Treplev says he flees conventional theater the way Maupassant fled the Eiffel Tower, which oppressed his mind with its vulgarity.

reading.ru: Вышел из третьего курса университета по обстоятельствам, как говорится, от редакции независимым.
reading.question: What does Treplev say about his own education and status?
options: He left university in his third year due to circumstances, and is independent of any editorial board
He graduated with honors
He was expelled for misconduct
He never attended university
reading.correct: He left university in his third year due to circumstances, and is independent of any editorial board
reading.explain: Treplev bitterly describes himself as having left university in the third year 'due to circumstances,' with no affiliation.

reading.ru: Сорок лет ему будет еще не скоро, но он уже знаменит и сыт по горло.
reading.question: How does the description characterize Trigorin's age and fame?
options: He is not yet forty but already famous and 'fed up to the throat' (jaded)
He is over sixty and long forgotten
He is a young unknown writer
He is exactly forty and retiring
reading.correct: He is not yet forty but already famous and 'fed up to the throat' (jaded)
reading.explain: The text says Trigorin won't be forty for a while yet, but he is already famous and sated/jaded.

reading.ru: Я без нее жить не могу.
reading.question: How does Treplev describe his feelings for Nina?
options: That he cannot live without her
That he can easily live without her
That he is unsure how he feels
That he only likes her as a friend
reading.correct: That he cannot live without her
reading.explain: Treplev declares that he cannot live without her.

reading.ru: Боялась, что отец не пустит меня.
reading.question: What was Nina afraid of on her way to see Treplev?
options: That her father would not let her come
That she would get lost in the dark
That the lake would flood
That she would miss the play entirely
reading.correct: That her father would not let her come
reading.explain: Nina says she was afraid her father would not let her come.

reading.ru: А меня тянет сюда к озеру, как чайку.
reading.question: What draws Nina to this place, according to her own words?
options: The lake draws her, like a seagull
The theater draws her
Treplev's mother draws her
The nearby town draws her
reading.correct: The lake draws her, like a seagull
reading.explain: Nina says she is drawn here to the lake, like a seagull — an image tied to the play's title.

reading.ru: Не забудь бы спирт и серу.
reading.question: What preparations does Treplev worry about forgetting for the play's special effects?
options: Alcohol/spirit and sulfur
Candles and matches
Costumes and makeup
Music and a curtain
reading.correct: Alcohol/spirit and sulfur
reading.explain: Treplev reminds himself not to forget the spirit and sulfur needed for the stage effect of red glowing eyes.

reading.ru: Вы, доктор, отлично знаете, что вам вреден сырой воздух.
reading.question: What health warning does someone give the doctor (Dorn) about his own habits?
options: That damp air is bad for him
That he smokes too much
That he drinks too much coffee
That he doesn't sleep enough
reading.correct: That damp air is bad for him
reading.explain: The character reminds Dorn that he, as a doctor, knows perfectly well that damp air is bad for his health.

reading.ru: Женщины всегда влюблялись в вас и вешались на шею.
reading.question: What does someone say about Dorn's history with women?
options: Women always fell in love with him and threw themselves at him
Women always avoided him
He never had any romantic success
Only one woman ever loved him
reading.correct: Women always fell in love with him and threw themselves at him
reading.explain: The speaker claims that women always fell in love with Dorn and threw their arms around his neck.

reading.ru: О, вы, почтенные старые тени, которые носитесь над озером в эту ночную пору, прилетите к нам.
reading.question: How does Nina's monologue in Treplev's play begin, addressing spirits?
options: Calling upon venerable old shades that hover over the lake at night to come to them
Calling upon the sun to rise early
Calling upon the audience to applaud
Calling upon her father to forgive her
reading.correct: Calling upon venerable old shades that hover over the lake at night to come to them
reading.explain: The monologue opens by invoking the venerable old shades that hover over the lake at night to fly to them.

reading.ru: Во мне душа Александра Великого и Цезаря, и Шекспира, и Наполеона, и последней пиявки.
reading.question: What does the 'World Soul' in Treplev's play claim to contain within itself?
options: The souls of Alexander the Great, Caesar, Shakespeare, Napoleon, and even the lowliest leech
Only the souls of great kings
The soul of one single unnamed person
Nothing at all, being empty
reading.correct: The souls of Alexander the Great, Caesar, Shakespeare, Napoleon, and even the lowliest leech
reading.explain: The World Soul declares that within it are the souls of Alexander the Great, Caesar, Shakespeare, Napoleon, and even the lowliest leech.
